title: Bitcoin fraud detection
summary: Exploring suspicious patterns in the Elliptic2 network, and the trade-offs behind a model’s predictions.
role: Group leader · R modelling and feature importance

sections.heading: The question
sections.body: How can graph-derived features help identify suspicious activity, and what does a positive prediction actually tell us? The group project compared Logistic Regression, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting on Elliptic2.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.body: I was the group leader for this academic project and contributed to modelling and feature importance in the consolidated R code. Random Forest impurity importance and Gradient Boosting relative influence helped describe how the models used their input features.

sections.heading: What needs a closer look
sections.body: The report describes an 80/20 split and three-fold cross-validation. A row-level split can put observations from the same network component into both training and test sets. Sampling nodes before building the graph can alter structural features differently by label. The script and report also use different seeds, so these reported results need to be reproduced from the same run.

sections.heading: The next useful test
sections.body: Hold out complete network components, document the evaluation population and save predictions from the same run. That would support a reproducible precision–recall curve and threshold comparison.

title: Q-learning grid world
summary: A small learning environment with obstacles and a teleport transition, exploring how rewards influence behaviour.

sections.heading: The environment
sections.body: A five-by-five grid contains a start, a goal, obstacles and a teleport transition. The code compares learning rates and plots episode rewards and state values.

sections.heading: What I explored
sections.body: How an agent learns through its reward signal, and how different learning rates affect the experiment.

sections.heading: The useful lesson
sections.body: A repeatable positive teleport reward can increase the score without the agent reaching the goal. Average reward and actual goal completion need to be checked separately.

sections.heading: What I would improve
sections.body: Use fixed random seeds, report goal completion separately and test for repeated reward loops. No reproducible performance benchmark is claimed here.
